title: Linear Inequalities in Two Variables

findings.finding: The opening review does not rehearse rearranging an inequality to isolate a variable, although this is the first step of the worked graphing example.
findings.breakdown: Students can complete the review by interpreting already isolated variables without demonstrating that they can rearrange 3x+4y>24 into an inequality in y. This algebraic step determines the half-plane to shade.
findings.checked: The supplied teaching is complete. The number-line review contains only isolated variables, and the linear-function review rehearses equations rather than rearranging inequalities. p4-solve-node demonstrates positive-coefficient inequality solving after the review, but does not provide review rehearsal. Negative-coefficient division has been removed from this finding: it occurs in guided practice rather than the worked example, and its teaching answer explicitly explains reversal.
findings.assumptions: Inequality rearrangement is prior learning, consistent with the course's Inequalities booklet. No calculator is needed.

repair.proposal: Add two short review items: 'Rearrange to make y the subject: a x+2y>6; b 3x+4y<=12.' Expected answers: a y>3-x/2; b y<=3-3x/4. These can fit alongside the existing review within one page.

findings.doneWhen: The opening review checks inequality rearrangement before students follow the worked graphing example.

findings.finding: Use a fixed boundary to compare equivalent inequalities, opposite half-planes and boundary inclusion.
findings.breakdown: The comparison makes students explain why an apparent change in inequality direction can preserve the region when both sides are negated.
findings.checked: All proposed regions are correct. p5 teaching and guided practice supply rearrangement, negative-division reversal, boundary inclusion and shading. The supplied practice does not contain this fixed-boundary comparison.
findings.assumptions: Students complete p5 guided practice before attempting the sequence.

repair.proposal: After p5-guided-block, before multiple inequalities, ask: 'Before solving, predict which questions give the same region and which include the boundary. Sketch: 1 x+y>4; 2 -x-y<-4; 3 x+y<4; 4 x+y<=4.' All have boundary y=4-x. Questions 1 and 2 shade above a dotted boundary; 3 shades below a dotted boundary; 4 shades below a solid boundary. Each comparison changes one feature: equivalent sign reversal, required side, then inclusion. Follow with: 'Sketch 2x-3y>=6.' Expected: solid boundary y=(2/3)x-2, shading below.

findings.doneWhen: Students predict and explain the comparisons, then correctly graph the unpatterned inequality.

findings.finding: Ask students to distinguish the intersection of boundary lines from membership in a system's solution region.
findings.breakdown: A boundary intersection is a solution only if it satisfies every inequality; excluding that point need not make the region empty.
findings.checked: The three proposed systems and expected regions are mathematically correct over real coordinates. Point testing, strict and inclusive boundaries, and intersection of half-planes are supplied by p4–p6. No additional method is needed.
findings.assumptions: The task is optional after p13-q12.

repair.proposal: Task: 'The lines y=x and y=-x meet at (0,0). Describe each region and decide whether (0,0) belongs: a y>=x and y>=-x; b y>x and y>=-x; c y>=x and y<=-x. Explain your decisions and give another solution to each system.' Expected: a on or above both lines, including the origin; b above y=x and on or above y=-x, excluding the origin; c x<=y<=-x, possible only for x<=0, including both edges and the origin. Another solution to a and b is (0,1); another solution to c is (-1,0).

findings.doneWhen: Students justify origin membership by checking both inequalities and show that all three systems have other solutions.

protectedGroups.observation: At the same x-coordinate, changing y moves a point from above the boundary to below it and changes whether it satisfies the inequality.
Shading unwanted half-planes and intersecting required half-planes identify the same solution set.

notReliablyReviewed.reason: Pages 12 and 14 were not attached. Their written diagram specifications support review of the task demands, but the visibility of the point labels and boundary styles could not be independently inspected.
